source.publication: 2025 Complete Income Tax Instruction Booklet (ip25), Kansas Department of Revenue, with Form K-40 and Schedule S bound in (PDF pages 19-22)
source.section: Form K-40 lines 1-12 (ip25 PDF page 20; exemption block PDF page 19); K-40 instructions lines 1-3 (PDF page 6), line 4 and exemptions (PDF page 6), lines 5-8 (PDF page 7); Schedule S line A10 (ip25 PDF page 21), instructions PDF page 11; FAQ 'Are Social Security benefits taxable to Kansas?' (https://www.ksrevenue.gov/faqs-taxii.html); WORKSHEET - Standard Deduction for People 65 or Older and/or Blind (PDF page 6); tax rate schedule: 2025 Tax Computation Worksheet (PDF page 34) and Tax Table (PDF pages 27-34)

worked: Federal AGI = IRA distribution (you) 100,000.00 + taxable Social Security 59,500.00 = 159,500.00. Federal taxable income = 159,500.00 - standard deduction 34,700.00 (31,500.00 + 2 x 1,600.00 for 65 or older) = 124,800.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Kansas starts from federal AGI). Schedule S Part A: line A1 0.00; lines A2-A8 0.00; line A9 total additions 0.00. Line A10 Social Security benefits included in federal AGI 59,500.00 (no income test for 2025); lines A11-A13 0.00; line A14 0.00; lines A15-A25 0.00; line A26 total subtractions = 59,500.00; line A27 net modification = 0.00 - 59,500.00 = -59,500.00. Form K-40: line 1 federal AGI 159,500.00; line 2 modifications -59,500.00; line 3 Kansas AGI = 159,500.00 + (-59,500.00) = 100,000.00; line 4 standard deduction (married filing joint), worksheet for people 65 or older: 2 boxes checked (you and spouse), 8,240.00 + 2 x 700.00 = 9,640.00 (the worksheet prints 9,640.00); line 5 exemption allowance (2 exemptions) 18,320.00, 0 dependents; line 6 total deductions = 9,640.00 + 18,320.00 = 27,960.00; line 7 taxable income = 100,000.00 - 27,960.00 = 72,040.00; line 8 tax (rate schedule as numbers, PDF page 34): 5.2% x 46,000.00 = 2,392.00 + 5.58% x (72,040.00 - 46,000.00 = 26,040.00) = 1,453.0320; total 3,845.0320 = 3,845.03. Line 7 is 100,000 or less, so the form reads the tax table: row 72,001-72,050, married filing joint column, PDF page 32, gives 3,844; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 9-10 do not apply (resident); line 11 0.00; line 12 total income tax 3,845.03. Credits (lines 13-15, 17): none, 0.00; state income tax = 3,845.03. Federal AGI is 159,500.00. The 75,000 Social Security income test in the FAQ is for years before 2024: for 2025 the whole 59,500.00 comes off at any income.
accepted_approximations: A pension from another state's government, private pensions, IRA and other employer-plan distributions and Roth conversions stay in Kansas income: no line subtracts them. This is read from the booklet's silence, not from a sentence saying they are taxed.
Tax is computed from the rates, not the printed tables and rounded worksheet subtraction.
